scope.included: High-recall first-pass catalogue of future-directed elements in the 66-book Protestant biblical canon, plus a small separately typed reception layer.
scope.warning: This is a catalogue, not a fulfilment scorecard. Inclusion records a candidate element; it does not establish pre-event dating, historical fulfilment, supernatural causation or theological authority.

candidacyScale.yes: The passage plainly presents a future-directed oracle, prediction, warning, promise or vision within its own literary frame.
candidacyScale.maybe: Future reference is present, but whether the element is predictive prophecy rather than blessing, rhetoric, typology, apocalyptic symbolism or later reception is materially disputed.
candidacyScale.low-probability: A prophetic reading exists, but it requires substantial extension beyond the passage's most immediate literary sense. This label concerns candidacy as a prophecy element, not the probability that God exists or acted.

zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Ruth: Blessings and providential narrative are present, but no distinct future-directed oracle was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.1 Chronicles: The principal prophetic elements duplicate Samuel-Kings parallels already catalogued; parallel witnesses will be linked during atomization.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Ezra: Prophets and fulfilled commands are reported, but no distinct quoted future oracle was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Nehemiah: Covenant warnings are recalled retrospectively; no distinct new future oracle was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Esther: No explicit prophetic oracle or future vision was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Proverbs: General future consequences are wisdom maxims rather than bounded prophetic claims in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Song of Solomon: No explicit future-directed oracle was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Galatians: Eschatological consequences occur, but no distinct prediction beyond parallel Pauline elements was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.Philemon: No explicit prophetic oracle or future vision was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.2 John: Warnings are present, but no distinct future prediction beyond the 1 John antichrist tradition was admitted in v1.
zeroRecordCanonicalBooks.3 John: No explicit prophetic oracle or future vision was admitted in v1.

records.element: Continuing conflict between the serpent and the woman's offspring, culminating in reciprocal wounding.
Canaan's descendants will be subordinated to the lines of Shem and Japheth.
Abram will become a great nation and acquire a great name.
The families of the earth will receive blessing through Abram.
Abram's descendants will live as aliens and be oppressed for four hundred years.
The enslaving nation will be judged and Abram's descendants will depart with possessions.
A fourth generation will return when Amorite iniquity reaches its stated limit.
Kings will arise from Abraham's lineage.
Sarah will bear a son and become ancestor of nations and kings.
Rebekah's twins will become two divided peoples, with the elder serving the younger.
Rulership will remain associated with Judah until the disputed coming of Shiloh or tribute-bearer.
A ruler from Israel will be exalted above Agag and the kingdom strengthened.
A star and scepter from Jacob will defeat Moabite leadership.
Edom and Seir will become possessions while Israel exercises dominion.
Ships from Kittim will afflict Asshur and Eber before their own destruction.
God will raise prophets like Moses from among Israel, whose words require obedience.
Covenant violation will result in foreign rule, dispersion and exile.
After exile and return to God, Israel will be gathered, restored and renewed.
Pharaoh's resistance will be answered by multiplied signs and judgments culminating in Israel's departure.
Egypt's firstborn will die in a final night judgment after which Israel is expelled.
Persistent covenant violation will escalate into defeat, desolation and exile, while confession permits covenant remembrance.
Eli's priestly house will lose longevity and be replaced by a faithful priestly line.
Irreversible judgment will fall on Eli's house for tolerated wrongdoing.
A human king will conscript, tax and appropriate the people's labor and property.
David's offspring will build a temple and David's dynasty and throne will be established enduringly.
Violence and public sexual humiliation will arise within David's own household.
Most of Solomon's kingdom will be transferred to Jeroboam while one tribe remains for David's line.
A Davidic ruler named Josiah will desecrate Bethel's altar.
Jeroboam's dynasty will be destroyed and Israel eventually uprooted and scattered.
No rain or dew will fall for a declared period except by Elijah's word.
Hazael will become king of Aram and inflict severe violence on Israel.
Judah's royal treasures and descendants will be carried to Babylon.
Whoever rebuilds Jericho will do so at the cost of firstborn and youngest sons.
The campaign will succeed, but Sisera will be delivered into a woman's hand rather than Barak receiving the glory.
A previously barren woman will bear a Nazirite son who begins Israel's deliverance from Philistines.
Judah will not need to fight the approaching coalition because the attackers will destroy one another.
God's anointed king will receive the nations and defeat opposing rulers.
The faithful speaker will not be abandoned to Sheol or see corruption.
A mocked and endangered sufferer will be delivered and remembered among the nations.
A zealous righteous sufferer faces unjust hatred and reproach before divine judgment.
The ideal royal son will rule justly, receive international tribute and bless all nations.
A royal figure at God's right hand will rule enemies and hold a Melchizedek-like priesthood.
A rejected stone becomes the chief cornerstone in a divinely made reversal.
Job expects a living vindicator and a future encounter with God despite bodily destruction; the temporal and resurrection sense is disputed.
God will bring every deed, including hidden deeds, into judgment.
Zion's punishment will end while Edom's wrongdoing is exposed and punished.
The Aram-Israel coalition against Judah will fail and Ephraim will eventually be shattered.
A child called Immanuel functions as a time sign for the removal of two kings and coming Assyrian distress.
A royal child will establish an enduring Davidic government of justice and peace.
A Spirit-endowed ruler from Jesse will judge justly and inaugurate extraordinary peace.
Babylon will be overthrown, with the Medes named among the attackers.
Egypt and Assyria will join Israel in worship and blessing.
God will prepare a feast, remove disgrace and swallow up death.
Exile will end and God will lead a restored people home by a prepared way.
Cyrus is named as the ruler who will enable Jerusalem and the temple to be rebuilt.
A rejected and suffering servant will bear others' wrongdoing, die, and afterward be vindicated and allotted a portion.
Nations and kings will bring wealth to a restored and radiant Zion.
God will create new heavens and earth marked by longevity, security and peace.
Judah and surrounding nations will serve Babylon for seventy years, after which Babylon is punished.
After Babylon's seventy years, the exiles will be visited and gathered home.
Hananiah will die within the same year.
Israel and Judah will be restored under a Davidic ruler after distress.
A new covenant will internalize divine instruction and bring comprehensive forgiveness.
A righteous Davidic branch and continuing priestly service will accompany restored Judah.
Babylon will fall to northern attackers while Israel and Judah return and seek covenant renewal.
Jerusalem's prince and inhabitants will go into exile, dramatized by Ezekiel's sign-act.
Jerusalem's siege begins on the very day identified by the oracle.
Nebuchadnezzar and many nations will attack Tyre, destroy its structures and leave it exposed.
Egypt will be desolate and dispersed for forty years before a diminished restoration.
Israel will be gathered, cleansed, internally renewed and restored to a fruitful land.
Judah and Joseph will be reunited as one people under one Davidic shepherd.
Gog's multinational invasion will be defeated by extraordinary divine judgment.
A measured temple, reordered land and life-giving river characterize a future restored order.
Four successive kingdoms will be displaced by an enduring kingdom established by God.
Four beastly kingdoms culminate in a persecuting ruler, judgment and dominion for the holy ones.
A ram identified with Media-Persia is defeated by Greece, followed by division and a desecrating ruler.
Seventy sevens encompass restoration, an anointed figure, destruction, covenant conflict and desolation.
A detailed sequence of Persian and Greek-era rulers culminates in a temple-desecrating northern king.
The northern king's final campaign ends between the sea and holy mountain without aid.
After unparalleled distress, the dead awaken to divergent destinies and the wise shine.
Time, times and half a time, 1290 days and 1335 days mark stages around desecration and deliverance.
Jehu's dynasty will be punished and Israel's military power broken in Jezreel.
After deprivation, Israel will return and seek God and David their king.
God's Spirit will be poured out broadly before the day of the Lord, accompanied by signs and deliverance.
Israel will be sent into exile beyond Damascus despite its worship.
David's fallen booth and Israel's fortunes will be restored with durable settlement.
Edom will be brought down and dispossessed while Zion is restored.
Nineveh will be overthrown after forty days, with the narrative treating repentance as grounds for reprieve.
Zion, Jerusalem and the temple mount will be devastated because of leadership corruption.
A ruler for Israel will emerge from Bethlehem and shepherd in security and peace.
Nineveh will fall violently and be exposed as judgment for imperial violence.
The Chaldeans will be raised as a rapid and violent instrument of judgment.
Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush and Assyria face differentiated judgments.
A cosmic and international shaking will bring greater glory and peace to the latter temple.
Zion's humble king will arrive on a donkey and extend peaceful rule to the nations.
A rejected shepherd is valued at thirty silver pieces, which are thrown to the potter in the temple.
Jerusalem will mourn over a pierced figure amid deliverance and transformation.
A day of conflict, divine intervention, geographic change and universal worship will center on Jerusalem.
A messenger will prepare the way before the Lord's sudden temple visitation and purifying judgment.
Elijah will be sent before the great day of the Lord to turn intergenerational relationships.
Jesus' assembly will be built and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
Jesus repeatedly predicts his Jerusalem suffering, death and resurrection on the third day.
The Jerusalem temple complex will be dismantled stone from stone.
The described coming and gathering signs are associated with 'this generation' not passing away.
Peter will deny Jesus three times before the cock crows.
Jesus' followers will face councils, rulers, family betrayal and widespread hatred while testimony spreads.
Jerusalem will be surrounded, devastated and its inhabitants killed or exiled.
Jesus' destroyed 'temple' will be raised in three days, interpreted narratively as his body.
One of Jesus' table companions will betray him, with Judas identified in the scene.
After Jesus' departure, the Spirit will come to teach, remind and guide the disciples.
Peter's future death will involve being led where he does not wish to go.
Agabus predicts a severe famine across the inhabited world during Claudius' reign.
Agabus predicts that Paul will be bound in Jerusalem and handed to Gentiles.
The ship will be lost and run aground, but every person aboard will survive.
After a partial hardening lasting until Gentile fullness, all Israel will be saved.
The dead will be raised and living believers transformed at the final trumpet.
At the Lord's descent, dead believers rise and the living are gathered with them.
Rebellion and revelation of a lawless figure precede the Lord's coming and that figure's destruction.
In later times some will abandon the faith for deceptive teachings and ascetic prohibitions.
Scoffers will question the delayed coming before a final cosmic judgment and renewed creation.
Human beings will appear before Christ's judgment seat and receive according to embodied deeds.
A future fullness will gather all things in heaven and earth into Christ.
The returning savior will transform believers' humiliated bodies into conformity with his glorious body.
When Christ appears, those whose life is hidden with him will also appear in glory.
The last days will include difficult times marked by an enumerated pattern of corrupt behavior and deceptive religion.
Believers await the glorious appearing of Jesus Christ while living disciplined lives.
A promised final shaking removes created things so that an unshakable kingdom remains.
The Lord's coming and judgment are near, reversing oppression by the rich.
Judgment is ready for living and dead and begins with God's household.
An expected antichrist is associated with present antichrists and a future appearing of Christ.
The Lord comes with holy ones to execute judgment on ungodliness.
Ephesus' lampstand will be removed unless the community repents.
Smyrna will experience imprisonment and affliction for ten days, with life promised to the faithful.
Philadelphia will be kept through or from an approaching worldwide hour of trial.
Conquest, war, scarcity and death unfold as the first four seals open.
The sixth seal brings cosmic and terrestrial upheaval and universal fear of judgment.
A sequence of trumpet judgments damages land, sea, fresh water, heavens and humanity.
The holy city will be trampled by nations for forty-two months.
Two witnesses prophesy for 1260 days, are killed, revive after three and a half days and ascend.
A woman and her offspring face dragon persecution, with wilderness protection for 1260 days or three and a half times.
A blasphemous beast exercises authority for forty-two months and persecutes the holy ones.
A second beast enforces worship and commerce associated with the first beast's name or number 666.
Kings are gathered by deceptive spirits to the place called Armageddon for the great day.
Seven kings and ten horns participate in a short-lived alliance that turns against Babylon and yields to the beast.
Babylon the great falls suddenly, ending its commercial and imperial dominance.
The beast and false prophet are defeated by the returning rider and their armies destroyed.
Satan is bound for one thousand years while martyrs reign, followed by release, final revolt and defeat.
The dead are judged before the great white throne and death and Hades are abolished.
A new heaven, new earth and New Jerusalem bring divine presence, healing and the end of death and curse.
The 1260-year period, anchored by Newton around AD 800, will not end before AD 2060 and may end later.
Daniel's 2300 days, read as years, terminate around 1843-1844 in the expected advent and cleansing.
